title: Small Talk
objectives: Talk about the weather (It's hot/cold/nice today)
Ask about someone's weekend/week (How was your weekend?)
Make casual conversation at work or in public
Keep a conversation going with follow-up questions

phrases: How's it going? / How are you?
target_language.grammar_pattern:
Past Simple (for weekends/yesterday):
- What did you do?
- I went to...
- I saw...
- I had...

Present for weather/now:
- It's hot
- It's raining
- The weather is nice

Examples:
- How was your weekend?
- It was good. I went to the park.
- What did you do?
- I saw a movie.

grammar_patterns.label: Asking about the weekend
examples: What did you do this weekend?

story.context: It's Monday morning. You see your coworker Sarah at work. You make small talk.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good morning! I'm good, thanks. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: I'm doing well. It's a nice day today, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes! The weather is beautiful. Not too hot.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It was good! I went to the park with my family. How about you?

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: That sounds nice! I stayed home and watched movies. It was relaxing.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That sounds fun! What movies did you watch?

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: I watched a new comedy. It was really funny!

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Cool! Well, have a good day!

speaking.title: Task 1: Talk about the weather
speaking.instruction: Record yourself making small talk about today's weather.
speaking.example: Hi! How are you? It's a nice day today, isn't it? The weather is beautiful. Not too hot or cold.

speaking.title: Task 2: Weekend conversation
speaking.instruction: Record yourself answering: How was your weekend? What did you do?
speaking.example: My weekend was good! I went to the park on Saturday. On Sunday, I stayed home and watched TV. It was relaxing. How was your weekend?

writing.title: Task 1: Write about your weekend
writing.instruction: Write 5 sentences about what you did last weekend.
writing.example:
1. My weekend was great.
2. On Saturday, I went shopping.
3. I bought new clothes.
4. On Sunday, I visited my friend.
5. We had dinner together.

writing.title: Task 2: Small talk conversation
writing.instruction: Write a conversation (10-12 lines) where you make small talk with a coworker. Include: greeting, weather, asking about their weekend.
writing.example:
You: Good morning!
Coworker: Good morning! How are you?
You: I'm good, thanks. How about you?
Coworker: Doing well! It's cold today, isn't it?
You: Yes, very cold! How was your weekend?
Coworker: It was good. I went to the movies.
You: That sounds fun! What movie did you see?
Coworker: I saw the new action movie.
You: Cool! Was it good?
Coworker: Yes, I loved it!
You: Nice! Well, have a good day!
Coworker: Thanks! You too!

sections.title: Why do we talk about weather?
sections.question: Why is weather such a common topic?
sections.explanation: In English-speaking cultures, weather is a safe, neutral topic to start conversations. It's polite small talk before deeper conversation. Everyone experiences weather, so it's easy to relate to.

sections.title: Past Simple for past events
examples: I went to the park (go → went)
sections.question: How do we talk about the past?
sections.explanation: For completed past actions, we use Past Simple. Many common verbs are irregular (went, saw, had). In questions, we use 'did' + base verb.

sections.title: Keeping conversation going
sections.question: How do we keep conversations flowing?
sections.explanation: Good conversations involve: asking back ('How about you?'), showing interest ('That sounds fun!'), and asking follow-up questions. This shows you're listening and engaged.

quiz.question: It's Monday morning. Your coworker says 'Good morning!' What do you say?
quiz.explanation: We greet back and often ask 'How are you?' to be friendly.

quiz.question: You want to ask about someone's weekend. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'How was your weekend?' is the correct question.

quiz.question: Someone tells you about their weekend. You want to show interest. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'That sounds fun!' shows genuine interest and keeps the conversation going.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: It ___ hot today.
quiz.explanation: 'It is hot today' is correct. We use 'is' with 'it' for weather.

quiz.question: Someone asks 'How was your weekend?' You had a good weekend. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'It was good' is correct. We use past tense to talk about the weekend (which is past).

quiz.question: You want to ask what someone did yesterday. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'What did you do yesterday?' is the correct past question.

quiz.question: Someone tells you about their weekend. You want to ask them a question back. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'How about you?' politely asks them to tell you about their weekend too.

quiz.question: It's the end of your conversation. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'Have a good day!' is a friendly, polite way to end conversation.

quiz.question: Write a 6-8 line small talk conversation. Include: greeting, weather, and asking about their weekend.
quiz.explanation: Use phrases like: 'How are you?', 'It's [weather]', 'How was your weekend?', 'That sounds fun!'

quiz.question: What topics are common for small talk in your culture? How is it different from or similar to American small talk?
quiz.explanation: Think about cultural differences in casual conversation. What's polite to ask about? What topics are avoided?

somali.description: Baro wada-hadalka fudud ee caadiga ah (small talk)
objectives: Waydii qofka wiigiisii (How was your weekend?)
Samee sheeko caadi ah goobta shaqada ama meelaha dadweynaha
Ku sii wad sheekada su'aalo dabagal ah

sections.explanation: Dhaqamada Ingiriisiga lagu hadlo, cimiladu waa mawduuc ammaan ah oo dhexdhexaad ah oo sheekada lagu bilaabo. Waa sheeko fudud oo edeb leh ka hor wada-hadal qoto dheer. Qof walba cimilada wuu la kulmaa, sidaas darteed way fudud tahay in laga sheekaysto.
Falalka dhammaystiran ee la soo dhaafay, waxaan isticmaalnaa Past Simple. Falal badan oo caadi ah qaanuun ma laha (went, saw, had). Su'aalaha, waxaan isticmaalnaa 'did' + falka aasaasiga ah.
Sheekooyinka wanaagsan waxay leeyihiin: dib u waydiin ('How about you?'), xiiso muujin ('That sounds fun!'), iyo su'aalo dabagal ah. Tani waxay muujinaysaa inaad dhegaysanayso oo aad danaynayso.
